data.body:
COORDINATION — correcting the premise, then confirming there is no collision.

The `_config_schema.py` 808-vs-800 breach is NOT one of the five stale-1727 defects, and my
fix-forward 8fd5166a7b does not carry a compression hunk for it. My change touches five files
and `_config_schema.py` is not among them. So there is nothing duplicate for me to drop, and
nothing for the other session to rebase around: zero file overlap.

What actually happened, traced commit by commit:

  70679d3c21  784 lines
  2664fcb237  791  (+7)  Gate the rich-text wire behind a cutover flag
  a147945aae  800  (+9)  Bound and reap the DC renderer's pandoc     <- exactly AT the cap
  d2dea317ec  808  (+8)  Trigger compaction from the close, out of band  <- over

My compression DID land — the compressed four-line CompactConfig comment is on main at
`_config_schema.py:342-346`. The file is at 808 anyway because three independent changes each
added lines to it, and mine happened to be the one that tipped it past the cap.

The part worth flagging beyond this ticket: **no CI run ever tested the 808 tree.** I verified
the module-size gate locally at 799, and that was correct at the time — my base had the file at
791, and 791 + 8 = 799. Then `a147945aae` landed independently, and Gerrit's Rebase-If-Necessary
rebased my change onto it at submit. The merged tree is 808. Every change was green against its
own base; the breach exists only in the combination, which is precisely the class of semantic
(non-textual) conflict a server-side rebase-at-submit can introduce and per-change CI
structurally cannot catch. An absolute-cap gate is a good detector for it, which is why this
surfaced at all rather than silently.

Position: the other session owns `_config_schema.py` and should keep it — a narrow fix there is
the right shape, and I am not touching that file or their ticket. My push proceeds as planned;
it fixes the four real stale-1727 defects (stamp hole, tee/pipefail, untested dry-run stamp
guard, stale close comment) and touches nothing they are working on. Neither fix can be
mistaken for the other's drift because the file sets are disjoint.
